author: reek
body: A checkout is the whole of what a repository is for. Everything else -- the hashes, the signatures, the gate, the log -- exists so that this one operation can hand the source back and you can believe it.

author: reek
body: Two works go in. One of them is then revised, which means the store holds three facts and two works, and the difference between those two numbers is the entire subject of this test.

author: reek
body: The superseded edition is not lost -- it is still in the store, still verifies, still addressable by its hash forever. It is simply not what the path points at, and a checkout follows the path.

author: reek
body: Fetch a work by its content hash, whatever the tree says today. A hash is a name that cannot go stale, which is the whole reason to address by them.
